lines.li: [us] How long will your people stay?
[them] Until the road calls, or until you ask us to go.
[us] Nobody's asking.
[them] Then we'll see what the road says.
[us] You came back.
[them,their:tribal] Our feet remembered the way.
[them] Your land was good to us, so here we are.
[us] It still is.
[them] Sit at our fire a while, if you like.
[us] I might, when the work's done.
[them] We'll keep a place for you.
[them] A wet camp is a quiet camp, everyone stays under cover.
[us] Stay dry if you can.
[them] We've slept wetter.
[them] Cold nights on the ground, the fire's all we have.
[us] Keep it high, then.
[them,their:tribal] We will, and the spirits will keep the rest.
[them] We will, and we'll sleep close.
[us] Is it a hard life, always on the road?
[them,their:tribal] The road is our home, as the fire is yours.
[them,their:medieval] Hard enough, but every town's a new market.
[them] Hard some days, but you see a lot of the world.
[us] I've not seen much of it myself.
[them] Then you've a lot left to see.
[us] Is the hunting any good round here?
[them,winter] The cold brings the herds down, so yes, for now.
[them] Good enough that we stayed.
[us] Leave some for us, then.
[them] We only take what we can carry.
[them] What do your people hunt with, out here?
[us,lowtech] Bows, mostly, and patience.
[us] Whatever we've got to hand.
[them] A hunter is mostly patience, whatever they carry.
[us] Where were you before all this?
[them] A place with a roof and a door, and that's all I want to say about it.
[us] You don't have to say more.
[them] Thank you for letting us stop.
[them] We won't stay longer than we're welcome.
[us,trait:Kind] Stay as long as you need.
[us] We'll see how it goes.
[them] That's more than most places say to us.
[us] Found anything yet?
[them] Nothing worth carrying, which is what we say right up until we do.
[us] And then?
[them] Then we say even less.
[them] Your ground is harder than it looks.
[us,us:best:Mining] I've dug enough of it to know.
[us] We've noticed.
[them] Hard ground keeps its secrets, that's why we like it.
[us] Where does your road end?
[them,samefaith] At a shrine of our faith, and yours, I think.
[them] At a shrine most of your people would walk past.
[us] And when you get there?
[them] We turn round and walk home, lighter.
[them] We pray for the places that let us rest.
[us] Then I hope ours is in your prayers.
[them] It is now.
[them] Have you had a look at the stall yet?
[us] Not yet, what have you got?
[them] A bit of everything, and fair prices for all of it.
[us] I'll come by.
[us] How's trade been on the road?
[them,their:medieval] Slow at every market but the last one, as always.
[them] Up and down, like the road.
[us] And here?
[them] Ask me when we've packed up.
[us] Is it true you can mend anything?
[them] Anything iron, and most things that aren't, given a day.
[us] I'll remember that.
[them] You've a crafter's way about you, I can tell.
[us] Is it that obvious?
[them] It's in how you watch the work.
[us] Do you ever get lonely out here?
[them] Lonely is a town full of people who don't listen.
[us] I'll leave you be, then.
[them] You can stay, you're quiet enough.
[us] Have you got wood enough for the winter?
[them] I'll manage, I always have.
[us] Ask, if you need it.
[us] Do you charge for what you do?
[them] We take what people can spare, and nothing from those who can't.
[us] That's generous.
[them,their:tribal] It is how the old healers taught us.
[them] It's how we were taught.
[them] You're favoring something, come and let me look at it.
[us] It's nothing.
[them] Everything's nothing until it isn't.
[us] What are you carrying on those poles?
[them] Relics of our faith, older than any of us.
[us] Can I see them?
[them,samefaith] Of course, they're yours as much as ours.
[them] From a respectful distance, yes.
[them] We walk so that others don't have to, that's how my mother put it.
[us] Walk where?
[them] Wherever the relics are needed next.
[us] What's the play about?
[them,their:tribal] A hunter who chases the moon, and catches it.
[them] A king who loses everything and finds it was never his.
[us] Does it end well?
[them] Depends who you ask afterward.
[them] They tell me you make things people stop to look at.
[us] Sometimes.
[them] Then you know what we're about.
[us] What are you measuring?
[them] The hills, the valleys, the way from here to the next town.
[us] What for?
[them] So the next people out here don't get lost.
[them] Your colony will be on the map now, properly.
[us] We've been here long enough.
[them] Long enough to be a landmark.
[us] Catching much?
[them,morning] They're biting, come back in an hour and I'll know.
[them] Enough to eat and some to salt.
[us] Good water, then.
[them] Do your people fish?
[us] When we have the time.
[them] Make the time, it's the only quiet work there is.
[us] What do you get out of those old ruins?
[them] Metal, mostly, and now and then something nobody's seen in a hundred years.
[us] Anything good this time?
[them] Ask me again when it's sold.
[them] Whoever built those ruins knew things we don't.
[us] Will anyone ever know them again?
[them] One salvaged piece at a time, maybe.
[us] How many farms do you work in a season?
[them] As many as the weather allows.
[us] Hard life.
[them] An honest one, though.
[them] You grow a good field, I'll say that.
[us] Thank you, it's most of my day.
[them] It shows in the rows.
[us] What happened to your ship?
[them] Something failed that shouldn't have, and we came down hard.
[us] Can it be fixed?
[them] Parts of it can be carried away, which is the next best thing.
[them] I keep looking up to see where we came from.
[us] Can you see it?
[them] No, but I know where it is.
[us] What do you expect the monolith to do?
[them] Nothing, we hope, and we write that down every night.
[us] And if it does something?
[them] Then you'll want us here to write that down too.
[them] Our elders say such stones were set by the old powers.
[us] Do you believe them?
[them] I believe it's worth watching.
[us] Where did you get animals like these?
[them] Some we raised, some we traded for, and one followed us home.
[us] Which one?
[them] The big one, and it's never left.
[them] You keep a good herd yourselves.
[us] They keep us as much as we keep them.
[them] That's the truth of it.
[us] How do you train them?
[them] Patience, treats, and losing a lot before you win.
[us] Sounds like raising children.
[them] Less shouting, mostly.
[us] How far do you carry the salt?
[them] From the flats to the hills, and back with whatever the hills will trade.
[us] Long road.
[them] Salt keeps, so we can take our time.
[them] In this heat a beast drinks twice what it carries.
[us] Rest them, then.
[them] We'll move them at night, it's kinder.
[us] Where are you from, really?
[them] Beyond the mountains, where the markets never close.
[us] Is it as far as it sounds?
[them] Farther, and every step of it worth it.
[them] In my country we give a gift before we talk of prices.
[us] And here?
[them] Here I will give you a good price instead, it is the same thing.
[us] Where are you taking them?
[them] To market, if the grass holds out and the weather lets us.
[us] Good grass here?
[them] Good enough to stop for, and that's high praise from a drover.
[them] Your beasts look well kept.
[us] We try.
[them] It shows in the coats.
[us] What is it you're walking for?
[them] For something done that can't be undone, only walked off.
[us] Does the walking help?
[them] Ask me at the end of the road.
[them] You keep our faith, so you know what this road is.
[us] I know it, though I've never walked it.
[them] May you never need to.
[us] What do you sing to them?
[them] What they need to hear, which is mostly that they're not alone.
[us] Do they answer?
[them] Listen tonight, by the old ones, and tell me they don't.
[them] The trees sleep now, so we sing softly.
[us] Do they hear it asleep?
[them] That's when they hear it best.
[us] Why travel alone?
[them] Healers who stay put get comfortable, and comfortable healers get careless.
[us] Doesn't the road get lonely?
[them] Every village has someone who needs me, so no.
[them] I hear {DOCTOR} is the one who sees to your sick.
[us,us:doctor] That's me, for my sins.
[us] That's right.
[them] Good, a colony needs a healer who stays.
[us] How long have you played together?
[them] Long enough to argue about every song.
[us] And you still travel together?
[them] The arguing is half the music.
[them] Come to our fire tonight, we're trying a new song.
[us] I might, if the work lets me.
[them] The work always says no, come anyway.
[us] I'm sorry for your loss.
[them] Thank you, and thank you for letting us rest.
[us] Who were they?
[them] Someone who'd have liked your colony, I think.
[them] I heard about {DEAD}, I'm sorry.
[us] Thank you.
[them] Grief walks with all of us, some days slower.
[us] What are you writing all day?
[them] Everything people remember, before they forget it.
[us] Is it that interesting?
[them] Everyone's story is, once it's written down.
[them] A colony that has lasted this long has a history worth writing.
[us] Then ask me anything.
[them] I'll start with the first day, if anyone remembers it.
[us] Where will you settle?
[them] Near enough to call you neighbors, if you'll have us.
[us] Good neighbors are hard to find.
[them] Then we'll try to be good ones.
[us] Thank you for standing with us.
[them,their:tribal] Your fight was our fight, as it should be between friends.
[them] Your fight was ours, the moment they came.
[us] We won't forget it.
[them] Good, we may need you one day.
[them] You look like you've been through it too.
[us] I'll mend.
[them] We all will, given a night's rest.
[us] What's the post for?
[them] To keep the road open, and to know who's on it.
[us] And who is on it?
[them] That's what we're here to find out.
[us] Where are you headed?
[them] Somewhere nobody asks where we've been.
[us] We won't ask.
[them] Then you're the first.
[them] If anyone asks, you never saw us.
[us] Who would ask?
[them] People who still think the war is worth it.
[them] I passed {CAMP} on my way in.
[us] They're staying a few days.
[them,their:tribal] A camp on your land is a guest at your fire, our elders say.
[them] Travelers look after each other out here.
[them] I've half a mind to see what {CAMP} will buy.
[us] Ask them, they might.
[them] Other traders on the road always know your prices, that's the trouble.
[them] I see you host {CAMP} as well.
[us] They asked, and we had room.
[them] Hospitality to travelers is noted, even at court.
[them] {CAMP}, {TRADERS} and us, your colony is a crossroads these days.
[us] It feels like one.
[them] Crossroads grow into towns, given time.
